title: eviction-cascade-root-cause-hypothesis-and-action-plan
content:
Context:
Observed a multi-hour degradation across a subset of Dedicated GPU pools on 2025-02-13 morning US/PST. Symptoms were: sustained queueing on p99 request latency, growing pod churn (OOMKill + eviction cycles), and reduced effective throughput despite nominal GPU allocation. Customer-facing impact: transient 5-15s tail latency increases for high-concurrency tenants; no data loss but a measurable drop in tokens/s for reserved pools.

Why this doc exists (quick):
- Capture on-call triage notes + why we think the pool entered an "eviction cascade" state.
- Rough root-cause hypothesis and short-term mitigations that were executed.
- Action items for a follow-up runbook patch and longer-term runtime fixes.

Timeline (high level):
- 2025-02-13 05:12 UTC: SRE alert: pool-dedicated-us-west-3 had CPU and GPU utilization spike; autoscaler started adding pods but pod readiness probes failed increasingly. (INC-1729)
- 05:19 UTC: First human oncall (Marco) sees >30% increase in pod restarts; logs show repeated kernel OOM and process termination in runtime worker.
- 05:30 UTC: Temporary mitigation: scaled down burst-guest queue, evicted lowest-priority jobs, toggled autoscaler to conservative mode (scaleUpDisabled=true) to avoid uncontrolled scheduling.
- 06:05 UTC: Deployment of a hotfix to runtime that disabled eager KV cache prefetch for quantized models in the affected pool (PR #4523) — reduced memory pressure on affected pods.
- 07:00 UTC: p99 latency and pod churn trending down; pool back to expected throughput by ~08:00 UTC.

Signals and evidence collected:
- Node/gpu metrics: NVML memory pressure for several GPUs hit >95% for short bursts.
- Container logs: repeated allocations failing inside allocator -> fallback paths -> increased CPU usage and then kernel OOM events.
- Kube events: eviction events with reason "MemoryPressure" and a cascade pattern where eviction of 1 tenancy freed up partial memory but scheduler immediately packed new burst pods on same nodes.
- Autoscaler logs: scale decision loops triggered aggressively because of queue latency metric; policy allowed simultaneous scale-ups across many nodes.
- Samples: stack traces captured from core dump analysis pointed to runtime module handling quantized weight loading (fast path) allocating pinned buffers.
- Repro attempt: synthetic replay of small quantized model loads + 40% concurrent burst jobs reproduced eviction cascade on staging cluster within ~15 minutes.

Hypothesis (root cause, short):
Primary chain: aggressive autoscaler + burst job packing -> concentration of ephemeral quantized-model loads on a subset of nodes -> runtime eager prefetch and pinned allocations -> transient GPU memory fragmentation -> kernel OOMs on affected pods -> kubelet eviction marking -> scheduler immediate rescheduling back to same nodes -> eviction cascade.
Contributing factors:
- Autoscaler policy allowed wide parallel scale-ups without topology-awareness (no maxPerNode constraint).
- Runtime optimization: eager KV cache prefetch for some quantized model variants triggers large contiguous GPU allocations which fragment memory under load.
- No per-tenant soft reservation in pool; burst jobs had equal priority as reserved sessions in that pool.

Immediate mitigations executed (what helped):
1) Conservative autoscaler toggle: disabled parallel aggressive scale-up and added temporary maxScalePerInterval cap.
2) Priority eviction: bumped reserved-customer QoS for in-flight production reservations and evicted low-priority burst queue.
3) Runtime hotfix: turned off eager prefetch for quantized weights (PR #4523). This was the largest single drop in memory pressure.
4) Scheduler tweak: applied a soft anti-affinity hint to spread ephemeral jobs across nodes for the pool (taint + preferred affinity) — reduced re-packing on same nodes.

Why the cascade kept happening initially (notes):
- Scheduler heuristics and autoscaler feedback loop happily placed new pods on nodes immediately after small frees, not accounting for fragmentation or short-lived allocations.
- Kubelet eviction threshold was configured to be relatively aggressive to protect node stability; once a few pods OOMed, eviction propagated quickly especially under repeated allocation attempts.

Runbook draft: immediate play for oncall (short checklist)
- Detect: check pool-specific metrics: p99 latency, pod churn, NVML mem util spikes. Dashboards: /dash/pools/eviction-triage (add link to dashboards).
- Quick triage commands:
  - kubectl get pods -n dedicated-pool --selector=pool=dedicated-us-west-3 -o wide
  - kubectl describe pod <candidate> | grep -i evicted
  - ssh node && sudo journalctl -u kubelet | tail -n 200 | grep -i OOM
  - nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used,memory.total --format=csv -l 1
- Short mitigations:
  - flip autoscaler -> conservative-mode: api patch /autoscaler/pools/xxx {"scale_behavior":"conservative"}
  - bump QoS on reserved sessions: /admin/reservations --set-priority
  - drain earmarked nodes for heavy burst jobs and evict burst pods first: kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
- Escalate to SRE runtime lead if memory allocation traces show pinned allocations in the runtime module.

Post-incident action items (owners + rough ETA):
- (Elena) Add maxScalePerNode and maxScalePerInterval to pool policy and ship canary: ETA 2025-02-21.
- (Jonah) Add scheduler anti-affinity hint by default for pools with mixed reserved+burst tenants: ETA 2025-02-28.
- (Marco) Finish runtime patch to replace eager prefetch with lazy streaming allocator + add fragmentation telemetry: ETA 2025-03-07. (PR #4523 is baseline; follow-up changes pending.)
- (Samir) Create an integration test that replays quantized-model load pattern under burst to prevent regressions: ETA 2025-03-03.
- (Aisha) Update the SRE runbook and add a dedicated dashboard panel for "eviction cascade" early warning (alerts for NVML short spikes + repeated pod evictions): ETA 2025-02-25.

Runbook/Governance changes proposed (longer-term):
- Autoscaler rules must be topology-aware: limit per-node injection and prefer spread for short-lifetime jobs.
- Add soft reservations (GPU memory floor) for reserved capacity pools so burst jobs cannot fully starve the reserved allocations.
- Runtime: avoid any eager pinned GPU allocations during model load; use streaming/eager-fallback only when mem headroom is ample. Also surface fragmentation metrics.
- Scheduler: introduce fragmentation-aware packing signal from NVML / cgroup memory stats to decision layer.

Open questions / TODOs (triage notes):
- How frequent are kernels hitting fragmentation vs pure overall memory exhaustion? Need more NVML fine-grained trace.
- Can we implement a cheap heuristic to detect "fragile nodes" (high fragmentation) and mark them temporarily ineligible for new ephemeral pods?
- Should we classify some quantized model families as "high frag risk" and route them to isolated pools?

Appendix: reproducible test notes (staging)
- Command used to repro: run 40 concurrent clients targeting staging pool with small quantized model loader (script attached in linked artifacts). Repro completes in ~12-18 minutes.
- Key logs: attached core dump snippets and allocator traces (see linked_artifacts).
- Minimal reproducer: allocate pinned buffers of varying sizes while concurrently creating short-lived worker pods that load the same model.

Slack / comms summary (to be sent to #sre-dedicated):
"Heads-up: we observed an eviction cascade in dedicated-us-west-3 caused by aggressive scale-up + runtime eager prefetch for quantized models. Hotfix turned off prefetch; pool stabilized. Working on autoscaler and runtime changes. See INC-1729 and PR #4523 for details. Follow-up runbook changes planned by 2025-02-28."

Notes to self (handy heuristics):
- If you see repeated small NVML spikes with <5s intervals and growing pod restarts, suspect fragmentation not purely total memory.
- Fast temporary mitigation = reduce parallel scale-ups + spread ephemeral jobs.

Unresolved: ticket INC-1729 assigned to eng-sre lead for closure once postmortem and runbook changes merged.

-- end of notes (WIP) --
